pages.says: Russia summoned Estonia's envoy and warned of 'open war' over drones three days after Tallinn voted to close its road border with Russia from 1 December, and Estonia flatly denies the drone charge.
pages.weakest: The pull quote 'The bully is playing the victim', repeated in the Tallinn box.

pages.says: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three US-escorted tankers hit mines in Hormuz, but they named no ships, the US says the lanes are clear, and oil prices barely moved.
pages.weakest: Also On The Desk: the Bangladesh item has nothing to do with Hormuz.

pages.says: Wong and Albanese signed a treaty letting Singapore send captured CO2 to Australia for storage and widened their crisis-supplies pact to ten kinds of goods; the dependence runs both ways.
pages.weakest: 'Held since No. 171, now settled: the meeting's outcomes...'

pages.says: Whether a candle smokes depends more on the wick's salts than the 'clean' wax on the label; refined paraffin did best in a Danish test, and a luxury candle's price is mostly glass and brand.
pages.weakest: The deck about Estee Lauder and Trudon does not match the headline.

pages.says: Jensen Huang, back as Nvidia's chief, apologised to staff for an affair, and a Senate committee will question him on chip exports on 3 December while the shares fell back.
pages.weakest: 'The board took him back on Monday after the government gave it what its filing called input (No. 172).'
pages.reason: A cold reader never learns why Huang was removed or what the government's input was; say in the first two paragraphs why he left and why the Senate cares.
pages.fixed: Second paragraph now says he resigned amid a personal scandal the board is examining as a possible spying risk, and why Congress is involved; the repeated 'Congress wants its turn' trimmed after recheck.

pages.says: Ant Group released a free MIT-licensed 124B model that wakes a small slice of itself per word, so a 128GB home Mac can run it.
pages.weakest: 'bartowski's GGUF files, built with llama.cpp b12600... Q4_K_M at 80.39GB...'
pages.reason: The numbers paragraph assumes knowledge of GGUF, quantisation, FP8 and H200s; speed and the GLM-5.4 delay are each said twice.
pages.fixed: Numbers paragraph rewritten with quantisation and GGUF glossed; duplicate speed and Z.ai lines cut; Q3_K_M and NVFP4 glossed after recheck.

pages.says: Vivo's V80 goes on sale in Singapore at S$899 with a big battery, 3x zoom and Apple Watch support (after iPhone pairing); its chip is middling and it lacks wireless charging.
pages.weakest: Also On The Desk on the Y32 repeats the fourth paragraph.

pages.says: A 31-year-old independent watchmaker's tourbillon sold for nearly seven times its estimate at a record Phillips Hong Kong sale, showing money moving from big brands to independents.
pages.weakest: Also On The Desk restates the Christie's lot from paragraph five.

pages.says: Disney's Hexed and Focker-In-Law open over Thanksgiving, both forecast near US$40-50m, with critics far kinder to Hexed.
pages.weakest: 'Boxoffice Pro's earlier long-range forecast...' a third set of forecasts.

pages.says: A large Nordic study tied lots of fruit in the early teens to less Crohn's disease, but it cannot show cause and effect, and fruit at seven pointed both ways.
pages.weakest: Also On The Desk: 'Phones at night' is off the page's subject.

pages.says: Singapore will send under-16 Kpod reoffenders on a 24-week IMH programme, and children who come forward face no penalty.
pages.weakest: Chatter: 'PSLE choices, meanwhile, close at 4.30pm...'
pages.reason: The PSLE paragraph is a second story; the Chatter repeats it and quotes no one.
pages.fixed: PSLE moved to an Also On The Desk strip; Chatter now quotes the officials and the Pediatrics first author; repeated Ong line and study caveat cut after recheck.

pages.says: Brent fell to $88 on signs of US-Iran talks, weakening the case for another Fed rise even though real yields have not moved.
pages.weakest: 'Lean: lower into 9 December...' the Four are never introduced for a new reader.

pages.says: US headline inflation jumped with two oil spikes but core stayed in a narrow band, so the shock may pass without a spiral, though the Fed decides before the next figures.
pages.weakest: The Dashboard grid, hard to read as text.

pages.says: Juggling is learnable in weeks, and behind it sit a worldwide convention scene and siteswap, a notation that turns patterns into arithmetic.
pages.weakest: 'Jack Boyce... found the longest prime siteswaps in 1999; version 1.7.8 came out on 11 October.'

pages.says: Start with beanbags, clubs come mostly from German makers like Henrys, and spending past about £10 a ball only matters to advanced jugglers.
pages.weakest: 'Wes Peden, whom Flowtoys bills as voted the top juggler...'

pages.says: Juggling briefly grows grey matter while you learn but it fades when you stop, and a ninety-day start costs a few hundred pounds.
pages.weakest: The broken duplicated headline line.
pages.reason: Headline broken and misattributes Oxford scans to Draganski; the ninety-day total does not match its items.
pages.fixed: Headline repaired and credited to the Hamburg group; total corrected to about £160 with the Numbers-club option priced separately.

pages.says: A review argues activity and fitness predict lifespan far more than diet quality, though a Finnish twin study suggests genes explain much of the link.
pages.weakest: The 'sedentary muscle' line repeats a quote already used.

pages.says: A booking calendar of Singapore gigs and family shows led by Horrible Histories at KidsFest, plus Japanese exhibitions and events worth flying to, with booking deadlines.
pages.weakest: Still Held: 'Live Nation's pages confirm KATSEYE...'

pages.says: A wagyu hamburg counter opened at The Star Vista, Bonchon returns to ION in December, and Hansang moved to Great World.
pages.weakest: Chatter repeating the members' price a third time.
pages.reason: The members' price repeats four times, Hansang gets two menu paragraphs, and Bonchon's December return contradicts 'date not announced'.
pages.fixed: Members' price now once; Bonchon's return and unannounced date together; a verdict paragraph replaces the second Hansang menu; unsupported stat claim removed after recheck.

pages.says: Vietnam created a paid Culture Day to grow its cultural industries, and the government first planned a four-day weekend meant to get people spending.
pages.weakest: '477 votes to 489 present' reads like a scoreline.

pages.says: The ministry cut the four-day plan to one Tuesday to protect year-end orders; firms rebuilt long weekends where they could, and Britain and China show production usually wins.
pages.weakest: The Golden Week numbers paragraph goes back over the China point.

pages.says: South Korea dropped and restored its alphabet holiday as it moved from factories to culture exports, and the desk predicts Vietnam won't give Culture Day a long weekend before 2030.
pages.weakest: 'The state is adding days, not losing them... which this desk has not seen confirmed.'
